items.quote: 5:15 If a soul commit a trespass, and sin through ignorance, in the holy things of the LORD; then he shall bring for his trespass unto the LORD a ram without blemish out of the flocks, with thy estimation by shekels of silver, after the shekel of the sanctuary, for a trespass offering.
items.claim: The text says that a person who sins by mistake against the holy things of the LORD must bring a ram without blemish as a trespass offering. The ram's value is set in silver shekels, measured by the shekel of the sanctuary. Note: the document does not name its source. Calling it Leviticus 5:15 comes from model-prior and is unverified.
items.actor: a soul (an individual who commits an unwitting trespass)
items.action: brings a ram without blemish as a trespass offering
items.object: a ram without blemish out of the flocks, valued in shekels of silver
items.mechanism: The offender makes up for an accidental sin against sacred property by giving an unblemished ram, valued in silver by the sanctuary's shekel standard.
items.place: unspecified (sanctuary referenced as the standard for the shekel)

items.quote: 5:14 And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
items.claim: The text presents the trespass-offering rule that follows as words the LORD spoke to Moses.
items.mechanism: The rule is introduced as divine speech passed on through Moses.
